title: Acme Shop: saved carts
subtitle: Plan to let signed-in shoppers save a cart by name and restore it on any device. Approve it, or request changes on the page.
tldr: orders-api gets a `saved_carts` table and four `/v1/saved-carts` routes; the cart page gets a **Saved carts** panel that restores a saved cart into the live cart. It replaces the browser-only *Save for later* list. 7 steps; 3 open questions need your pick before I start.

sections.title: Context
sections.lead: Carts last 24 hours on one device; shoppers who plan a reorder lose them.

blocks.md:
Today a cart is a row in the `carts` table, keyed by the session cookie, deleted 24 hours after the last change (`services/orders-api/src/carts/expire.ts`). *Save for later* copies items into the browser's `localStorage` (`web/src/cart/saveForLater.ts`), so it doesn't follow the shopper to another device and vanishes when they clear the browser.

Support logged 41 tickets about lost carts in September. 63 % came from business accounts that reorder the same supplies each month.

sections.title: Approach
sections.lead: orders-api stores named carts per account; the web cart page lists them and restores one into the live cart.

blocks.title: Proposed: saved carts
blocks.caption: Amber dashed parts are new. Open **orders-api** to see the new routes next to the pricing code they reuse.

nodes.md: One row per saved cart: `account_id`, `name`, `lines jsonb`, `saved_total_cents`, `last_used_at`. Unique on `(account_id, name)`.

steps.label: The shopper names the cart and presses Save.
The panel posts the cart id and name to `/v1/saved-carts`.
orders-api copies the cart lines into `saved_carts`.
The panel asks orders-api to restore a saved cart.
orders-api reads the saved lines and stamps `last_used_at`.
orders-api writes the repriced lines into the live cart.
The cart page reloads the live cart with changed lines flagged.

sections.title: Steps
sections.lead: Seven steps, each one reviewable PR; the API lands before the UI.

items.title: Add the `saved_carts` table
items.md: New table only; no change to `carts`, so the migration takes no lock on live carts. Unique index on `(account_id, name)`; index on `last_used_at` for the sweeper.

items.title: Write `SavedCartRepo` with the 20-cart limit
items.md: `save`, `list`, `load`, `rename`, `delete`. Saving a 21st cart throws `SavedCartLimit`; saving under an existing name replaces that cart.

items.title: Add the four `/v1/saved-carts` routes
items.md: `GET /v1/saved-carts`, `POST /v1/saved-carts`, `POST /v1/saved-carts/:id/restore`, `DELETE /v1/saved-carts/:id`. All need a signed-in account; a session-only shopper gets `401`. The limit maps to `409 saved_cart_limit`.

items.title: Reprice restored carts and flag changed lines
items.md: `reprice()` takes saved lines and returns current prices plus `changed: true` on lines whose unit price moved. Discontinued SKUs are dropped and listed in `skipped`.

items.title: Build the Saved carts panel and the Save cart popover
items.md: Panel on the right of the cart at ≥ 900 px, under it below. The popover asks for a name, defaulting to the date. Restore asks before it replaces a non-empty cart.

items.title: Schedule the nightly sweeper
items.md: Deletes carts unused for longer than the retention you pick. Runs at 03:10 UTC, in batches of 1,000 rows.

items.title: Replace *Save for later* and turn the flag on
items.md: On first load with the `saved-carts` flag on, the web app offers to import the old `localStorage` list as a saved cart, then deletes it. Staff first for 3 days, then everyone.

sections.title: Open questions
sections.lead: Pick one option per question; my recommendation is starred. Your picks go with **Approve plan** or **Request changes**.

items.text: How long does a saved cart stay after its last use?
items.sub: Recommend 180 days: covers half-yearly reorders; the table stays under 2 GB.

choices.label: Until deleted
choices.md: No sweeper; the 20-cart limit is the only cap.

items.detail: **Why 180:** 70 % of business reorders in the last year came within 150 days of the previous order (orders DB, Sep 2025 to Sep 2026). At 1.2 M accounts and 1.4 saved carts per active account, 180 days keeps about 900,000 rows, about 1.8 GB. *Row size is an estimate; check it on staging in step 1.*

items.text: What does a restored cart charge when a price changed?
items.sub: Recommend today's price with a notice: the saved price could undercut a price rise.

choices.label: Saved price for 7 days
choices.md: Needs a price lock in pricing and a new discount reason.

items.detail: **Notice:** the panel badge says *Prices changed*; the cart marks each changed line with the old price struck through. **Keep** adds a price-lock path to `pricing/reprice.ts` and a finance sign-off; I'd ticket it if you want it later.

items.sub: Recommend signed-in accounts only: guests have no account to attach the cart to.

choices.label: Guests too, by email link
choices.md: Adds an email token flow and a mail template; about 3 more days.

items.detail: Guests are 22 % of carts but 6 % of repeat orders. A guest who presses Save cart gets the sign-in sheet, then the cart is saved.

sections.title: Risks
sections.lead: The main risk is shoppers reading a repriced cart as a bug.

rows: A restored total differs from the saved total; shoppers report it as a bug
Flag each changed line (step 4) and show *Prices changed* on the cart, if you pick the notice in question 2.
A saved cart holds a discontinued SKU
Restore skips the SKU and lists it above the cart; it never fails the whole restore.
The *Save for later* import runs twice on two tabs
Import is keyed by a hash of the list; a second import with the same hash is a no-op.
The 20-cart limit plus the sweeper cap it; alert above 3 GB.
